title: Cryoembedding Protocol
author: Malcolm Low
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.xidfka6

steps.title: Prepare Fixed Tissue
steps.instruction: Rinse fixed tissue (immersion or perfusion) in phosphate buffer (PB, 0.1M, pH 7.3) with increasing sucrose concentrations.

substeps.instruction: Rinse in 5% sucrose for 24 hours or until tissue sinks.
Rinse in 10% sucrose for 24 hours or until tissue sinks.
Rinse in 20% sucrose for 24 hours or until tissue sinks.
Note: Final sucrose concentration may vary from 5-30% depending on tissue requirements.

steps.title: Cool 2-Methyl Butane
steps.instruction: Cool 2-methyl butane in a dry ice bath until dry ice no longer boils when added.

steps.title: Create Embedding Molds
steps.instruction: Construct aluminum foil molds for tissue embedding.

substeps.instruction: Cut aluminum foil into small squares (approximately 1" square or less).
Form foil squares around the bottom of a small glass vial or appropriately sized mold.
Write all relevant tissue information on the foil while it is still on the mold.

steps.title: Prepare Tissue for Embedding
steps.instruction: Transfer tissue from sucrose to OCT.

substeps.instruction: Remove foil from the mold and add OCT.
Transfer tissue from 20% sucrose into a small dish or weigh boat containing OCT to remove excess sucrose.

steps.title: Embed Tissue in Mold
steps.instruction: Position tissue in the foil mold and cover with OCT.

substeps.instruction: Place tissue in the foil mold, ensuring it is flat on the bottom.

steps.title: Freeze Tissue Blocks
steps.instruction: Freeze the OCT-embedded tissue using 2-methyl butane.

substeps.instruction: Hold the mold in 2-methyl butane using forceps until the OCT freezes.
Avoid dropping the mold into the 2-methyl butane to prevent the block from freezing too fast and cracking.

steps.title: Store Frozen Blocks
steps.instruction: Store blocks in a freezer to prevent freeze-drying.

substeps.instruction: Keep blocks in a bucket on dry ice until ready for long-term storage.
Fold excess foil over the top of the block.
Transfer blocks to a -20ºC or -80ºC freezer.

steps.title: Process Fresh Tissue
steps.instruction: Handle fresh tissue blocks via snap freezing.

substeps.instruction: Snap freeze fresh tissue at approximately -40ºC.
Immediately section on the cryostat, or cover in OCT, snap freeze, and store for later sectioning.
